title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482) rent cap
requirement: Annual rent increases for covered units are limited to 5% plus the regional cost-of-living change, or 10%, whichever is lower; the maximum allowable increase was 8.9% from August 1, 2024 to July 31, 2025 (previously 8.8%).
coverage_conditions: Buildings older than 15 years, applied on a rolling basis. Excludes newer construction, deed-restricted affordable units, certain dormitories, owner-occupied two-unit properties, qualifying single-family homes and condominiums, and RSO units.
exemptions: Units built within the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable units; certain dormitories; two-unit properties with an owner-occupied second unit; qualifying single-family homes and condominiums; units already subject to the City's RSO.

title: Tenant Protection Act annual rent cap (Civ. Code § 1947.12)
requirement: A landlord may not raise the gross rent over any 12-month period by more than 5% plus the change in the cost of living, or 10%, whichever is lower, above the lowest rent charged in the previous 12 months, and no more than twice in 12 months.
key_value: 5% + CPI, or 10%, whichever is lower, per 12 months
coverage_conditions: All residential rental property, including units in mobilehome parks, subject to the listed exemptions; caps increases over any 12-month period and allows at most two increases in 12 months.
exemptions: Affordable deed-restricted housing; dormitories; housing under stricter local rent control; housing certified for occupancy within 15 years (not mobilehomes); separately alienable condos/homes owned by non-corporate owners with notice; owner-occupied two-unit properties; mobilehome owners.
quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.

program_notes: Affordable housing restricted by deed or government agreement for very low, low, or moderate income
Housing under local rent or price control restricting annual increases below the state cap

applicability.per_tenancy: New tenancy with no holdover tenant: initial rate is not capped. Mobilehome tenancies are covered only for increases on or after February 18, 2021. The separate-property exemption requires the written notice to tenants.
coverage_quotes: Housing that has been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless the housing is a mobilehome.

penalty: Owner liable for injunctive relief, damages equal to the excess rent charged, and discretionary attorney's fees, plus up to treble damages for willful, oppressive, fraudulent or malicious conduct; the Attorney General or local city attorney may enforce; three-year limitations period.

title: Tenant Protection Act just cause eviction (Civ. Code § 1946.2)
requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied residential real property for 12 months, the owner must not terminate the tenancy without just cause stated in the written notice; for no-fault just cause the owner must give one month's rent relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent.
key_value: 12 months' occupancy; 1 month's rent relocation or rent waiver
coverage_conditions: Residential real property occupied 12 months or more, except housing certified for occupancy within 15 years, single-family owner-occupied homes with no more than two units or bedrooms, owner-occupied two-unit properties, separately alienable property held by non-corporate owners, and deed-restricted affordable housing.
exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy; nonprofit hospital, religious, extended care, licensed elderly and adult residential facilities; school dormitories; housing certified for occupancy within 15 years; single-family owner-occupied residences and mobilehomes; owner-occupied two-unit structures; separately alienable property of non-corporate owners; deed-restricted affordable housing.
interaction: Yields to local just cause ordinances adopted on or before September 1, 2019, and to more protective local ordinances adopted or amended after that date; property is not subject to both.
quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.

program_notes: owner of separately alienable property who is not a real estate investment trust, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member
Housing restricted by deed or government agreement as affordable for very low, low or moderate income, or receiving housing subsidies
applicability.per_tenancy: Tenant must have continuously and lawfully occupied for 12 months or more (24 months or more for one tenant if additional adult tenants are added earlier); tenant sharing bathroom or kitchen with the owner-occupant is exempt; transient hotel occupancy is exempt.
coverage_quotes:
Housing that has been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15
years, unless the housing is a mobilehome.

penalty: Failure to comply renders the termination notice void; an owner who attempts to recover possession in material violation is liable for actual damages, discretionary attorney's fees, and up to three times actual damages for willful, oppressive, fraudulent or malicious conduct.

title: California security deposit cap and return rules (AB 12)
requirement: Since July 1, 2024, a landlord may charge no more than one month's rent as a security deposit; small landlords may charge two months. Deposits must be returned within 21 days with an itemized statement, and landlords must offer a move-out walk-through inspection.
key_value: 1 month's rent; 2 months for small landlords
coverage_conditions: All California residential tenancies. Landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total, held by a natural person, family trust, or LLC of natural persons, may charge two months' rent.
exemptions: Landlords owning only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total (natural person, family trust, or LLC with all natural-person members) may charge up to two months' rent.
quoted_span: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units

coverage_quotes: Starting July 1, 2024, landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total can charge up to two months' rent for furnished and unfurnished units if ownership is held by a natural person, family trust, or limited liability company (LLC) where all members are natural persons

title: California security deposit limit (Civ. Code § 1950.5)
requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security exceeding one month's rent, in addition to the first month's rent paid at occupancy, and must account for and return the remainder within 21 days after the tenant vacates. Small landlords (natural persons or family LLCs owning no more than two rental properties and four units) may charge up to two months' rent, unless the tenant is a service member.
key_value: 1 month's rent; 2 months' rent for small landlords
coverage_conditions: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling.
exemptions: Security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024; advance payment of six months' rent where the lease term is six months or longer; higher security for service members subject to written statement and return rules.
quoted_span: (c) (1) Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.

applicability.per_tenancy: Does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024.

penalty: A landlord who in bad faith fails to comply with the itemized-statement requirements is not entitled to claim any amount of the security.

title: Gov. Code § 12955 income and credit screening limits for renters
requirement: A landlord may not use income standards that ignore co-applicants' combined income or, with a government rent subsidy, standards not based on the tenant's rent share, and must accept verifiable alternative evidence of ability to pay in place of credit history.
coverage_conditions: All owners and housing providers of housing accommodations in California; applies to rental applications and tenancies, including those with government rent subsidies such as Section 8 vouchers.
exemptions: Nothing limits a landlord's ability to request information to verify employment, request landlord references, or verify the identity of a person. A landlord may still make a written or oral inquiry about the level or source of income.

the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.

applicability.per_tenancy: Applies to each rental application and tenancy; the credit-history and rent-share limits apply where there is a government rent subsidy, such as a Section 8 voucher.

title: FEHA criminal history and source-of-income screening protections
requirement: Landlords may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and may not blanket-ban applicants with criminal history. Conviction-based denial must be directly related to tenancy, and source-of-income discrimination, including refusing Section 8 vouchers, is barred.
coverage_conditions: Most housing accommodations in California and most housing providers, including landlords, tenant screening companies, apartment managers, and property management companies.
interaction: FEHA invalidates any state law to the extent it purports to require or permit unlawful housing discrimination.
citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
quoted_span: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system. Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.

applicability.per_tenancy: An owner occupying the home and renting to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics.

penalty: Remedies include out-of-pocket losses, injunctions, access to housing, emotional distress damages, civil penalties or punitive damages, and attorney’s fees.

sources.quoted_span: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system. title: Berkeley tenant screening fee disclosure and non-refundable application fee ban
requirement: An owner or agent who charges an applicant a screening fee must first give a tenant screening fee rights statement and the state maximum fee cap, and may not charge an existing tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy or to add or replace a roommate.
coverage_conditions: All residential rental agreements in Berkeley, regardless of any contrary lease language.
quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.

title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
requirement: Rental housing providers may not inquire about, require disclosure of, or use criminal history in advertising, applications, tenant selection or decisions, and may not refuse to rent, terminate a tenancy, or charge more based on criminal history.
coverage_conditions: All rental housing providers in Berkeley, except lifetime sex offenders, limited public housing/Section 8 exemptions, owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units, owner move-back units, and units where existing tenants sublet or add/replace roommates.
exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; public housing/Section 8 properties (limited exemptions); owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units; units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back under BMC 13.76.130 A.9; units where existing tenants sublet or add/replace roommates.
quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

program_notes: public housing and Section 8 properties (limited exemptions)
applicability.per_tenancy: Lifetime sex offenders; units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back under BMC 13.76.130 A.9; units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
coverage_quotes: Owner-occupied properties (between 1-3 units) in which an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence
Public housing/Section 8 properties limited exemptions

penalty: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation; civil damages including actual damages or three times one month's rent, punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.

title: Berkeley coordinated pricing algorithm ban
requirement: No one may sell, license, or provide to Berkeley landlords, and no landlord may use, a coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley.
coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords and to persons who sell, license or provide coordinated pricing algorithms, for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
exemptions: Products that publish aggregated, anonymous rental data without recommending rents; products for setting rent or income limits under affordable housing guidelines; and uses for market research for project financing, appraisals, or research, testing or training for software development.
quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley.

title: Los Angeles motion on algorithm-based rent-setting software
requirement: Would instruct the Los Angeles Housing Department to report on how many ownership and management entities use algorithm-based software to set rents and on the feasibility of banning that software's use to set rents in the City.
coverage_conditions: The City of Los Angeles; no building, unit or owner limits are stated.
citation: Los Angeles City Council Motion, C.F. 24-1031
quoted_span:
I THEREFORE MOVE that the City Council instruct the Los Angeles Housing Department to 
report on the number of ownership and management entities that are using algorithm-based 
software to establish rents and the feasibility of instituting a ban on the use of this software to set 
rents in the City.
